_status: PLACEHOLDER - Yenna owns this file. Every number below is a placeholder until she reviews it. How to measure, why we check and equipment are in measurements.json.
_how_to_read: Each band is [low, high]. A value below `low` or above `high` is at least that status; null means no limit on that side. The worst status wins. `label` and `unit` are shown on screen. `keywords` link a live vital to the red-flag text in protocols (a flag lights up when the vital is red and the flag text contains a keyword). This file keeps only ranges and sources.

hr_rest.label: Resting heart rate
hr_rest.source: Medical lead's sheet (proposed, not clinically validated), RULE-01

baseline._note: Above/below the frozen pre-flight usual (regions.json baseline.first_days). Sheet: +/-15 bpm (RULE-01, read as '+/-15 bpm from baseline', Yenna confirms). Rise above +10 bpm: team default (so slow drift +10..15 bpm shows as Watch).

hr_rest.qa_note: QA 2026-11-14: Resting HR <50/>90 and <40/>120 are stated as validated astronaut limits; not substantiated by general NASA standard. | Keep proposed baseline thresholds as DEMO ONLY; severe symptoms, consciousness and confirmed signal take priority over number.

actions.watch: Rest and repeat the pulse reading with good sensor contact. Check symptoms and record the trend.

sheet.baseline: 30-day pre-flight seated resting morning average HR (± 5 bpm)
sheet.watch: Resting HR < 50 bpm or > 90 bpm (or ±15 bpm baseline)

sheet.rationale: Cardiovascular deconditioning, fluid shift, dehydration, or acute arrhythmogenic stress

sheet.nominal: Cabin ppCO₂ < 2.0 mmHg (approx. < 2,600 ppm); nominal < 1.5 mmHg

red_flags._how_to_read: Red flags that can move an emergency protocol forward (see red_flag_routes in protocols). A flag is active when `metric` is below `below` or above `above` for at least `for_s` seconds, and the signal quality is at least `min_signal_quality` (so a slipped sensor is not read as a lost pulse). PLACEHOLDER numbers: Yenna reviews.

plausible._how_to_read: Values outside [low, high] are a measuring error, not a body state: shown as 'Invalid', never as a number, never judged, never alerted on. null = no limit. Live vitals and the PPG pulse rate.
plausible.source: PLACEHOLDER - plausibility limits agreed Nov 15; Yenna reviews

daily_targets._how_to_read: Behaviour targets for the daily missions (never health results). PLACEHOLDER: Yenna reviews.

cv._how_to_read: Unresponsive crew member detection (webcam + PPG, runs on the laptop, no video stored). Read by frontend/src/cv. In microgravity an unconscious person floats instead of falling, so every camera value is measured RELATIVE TO THE TORSO (origin between the shoulders, scaled by shoulder width): 'sw' = shoulder widths. unresponsive_score = weights x (limb stillness, neutral body posture, eyes closed, smooth drift, staring, still hand from PPG), 0 to 1. PLACEHOLDER: tune with the debug panel on /admin; Yenna reviews.

nbp._how_to_read: Neutral body posture (relaxed body in microgravity): elbows bent elbow_deg, wrists rise above the elbows by wrist_rise sw, upper arms raised upper_arm_raise_deg away from the torso line, wrists in front of the elbows by depth_margin sw (depth is noisy), held for hold_s. Scored against the person's own posture at calibration.

drift._how_to_read: Torso movement in the image, in sw/s (rotation counted in radians/s). Slow, steady drift (between min_speed and max_speed, with little wobble around a straight line) supports 'unresponsive'; jerky movement does not.

ppg._how_to_read: Pulse checks on the live vitals stream (works with or without the camera). Pulse lost = clip on with good contact (signal_quality at or above good_quality, baseline steady) but the pulse wave is flat (pulse_amplitude below flat_ratio x the person's recent amplitude) or no beats for no_pulse_s seconds, or the thresholds.json red flag named pulse_lost_red_flag. Clip off = signal_quality below clip_off_quality or the baseline jumps by more than baseline_jump_ratio. A long clean signal (quality at or above clean_quality for still_hand_s) means the hand is not moving.

fall._how_to_read: Fall detection runs wherever there is gravity: Moon base (1/6 g), Surface rover on the Moon (1/6 g) and Surface rover on Mars (0.38 g). Not on the ISS or in Mars transit (microgravity: an unconscious person floats, so only the body-relative signals count). Keys are env keys (rover:moon, rover:mars). Uses the image's 'down' because the camera there is mounted upright. Hips move down faster than hip_drop_speed sw/s, then the body stays still (image motion at or below still_motion sw/s) for still_after_s. PLACEHOLDER numbers, tuned for nobody yet; a fall on Mars is faster than on the Moon.

mars_surface.source: DRAFT: Curiosity RAD on the surface, 0.21 mGy/day = about 8.75 µGy/h (Hassler et al. 2014, Science 343:1244797). Only used if dose_mars_surface.json is missing.

pvt._how_to_read: Reaction test rules. Bands on pvt_median_ms / pvt_lapse_rate_pct are the population percentiles (pvt_norms.json). On top, with at least min_baseline_days of personal results, a median reaction time more than baseline_slower_pct slower than the personal baseline (median of the previous days, up to 30) is at least Watch. With fewer days, the population percentiles only.
pvt.act_now_note: None from the reaction test alone (Yenna's rule 12: pause safety-critical tasks, request crew assessment).

calories_pct.label: Calories eaten (of personal target)
calories_pct.no_data_note: No calorie log or target in the app yet: shown in Learn only, never judged.
calories_pct.qa_note: QA 2026-11-14: Fixed 2,500–3,200 kcal and 2.5L are not universal prescriptions; low intake alone not emergency. | Use astronaut-specific prescription; watch sustained deficits; urgent escalation depends on clinical dehydration/illness.

qa.finding: QA 2026-11-14: Fixed 2,500–3,200 kcal and 2.5L are not universal prescriptions; low intake alone not emergency.
qa.recommendation: Use astronaut-specific prescription; watch sustained deficits; urgent escalation depends on clinical dehydration/illness.

actions.watch: Review intake and hydration against individual plan; inform nutrition/medical crew if deficit persists.
actions.act: Notify the medical officer if severe dehydration, inability to eat/drink, or concerning symptoms occur.

sheet.baseline: NASA nutritional prescription based on BMR and individual body mass
sheet.watch: Caloric intake < 80% target or fluid < 2.0 L/day for 2 days
sheet.act: Caloric intake < 50% target for > 3 days or severe fluid deficit
sheet.rationale: Chronic negative energy balance accelerating muscle wasting and bone loss
sheet.escalation: Conditional; per rule branch and symptoms

calories_pct.source: Medical lead's sheet (proposed, not clinically validated), RULE-09

co2_mmhg.label: Cabin CO2
co2_mmhg.gap_note: Watch at 2.0 mmHg or more is a conservative engineering warning; Warning above 3.0 mmHg (NASA-STD-3001 Rev F [V2 6004] is a 1-hour average; the app compares single readings). Act now = mission CO2 alarm or crew symptoms, never a number. ppm = mmHg / cabin pressure x 1,000,000 (ISS 760 mmHg; Moon base and rover pressure: environments.json cabin_pressure_mmhg).
co2_mmhg.qa_note: QA 2026-11-14: NASA 2026 Vol2 Rev F specifies 1-hour habitat average <=3 mmHg; 2/4 are not validated medical severity categories. | Label 2 mmHg as conservative engineering warning only; 3 mmHg 1-hour requirement, off-nominal response mission-specific.

qa.finding: QA 2026-11-14: NASA 2026 Vol2 Rev F specifies 1-hour habitat average <=3 mmHg; 2/4 are not validated medical severity categories.
qa.recommendation: Label 2 mmHg as conservative engineering warning only; 3 mmHg 1-hour requirement, off-nominal response mission-specific.

actions.watch: Verify CO2 sensor, duration and local ventilation; notify life-support operators.
actions.act: Activate authorized environmental response for mission CO2 alarm or symptomatic crew; do not equate 4 mmHg with CO2 narcosis.

sheet.baseline: Vehicle ECLSS baseline environmental limit specification (NASA-STD-3001 Vol 2)
sheet.nominal: Cabin ppCO₂ < 2.0 mmHg (approx. < 2,600 ppm); nominal < 1.5 mmHg
sheet.watch: Operational early warning at ppCO2 >=2 mmHg (DEMO CONSERVATIVE) or rising trend
sheet.act: One-hour average cabin ppCO2 >3 mmHg violates NASA-STD-3001 Rev F nominal requirement [V2 6004]; environmental response per mission-specific procedures. Do not label 4 mmHg as CO2 narcosis.
sheet.rationale: Operational environmental threshold to prevent mild hypercapnic symptoms (headache, SANS); clinical CO₂ narcosis occurs at much higher levels.
sheet.escalation: Conditional; per rule branch and symptoms

co2_mmhg.source: Medical lead's sheet (proposed, not clinically validated), RULE-17

radiation_msv.label: Radiation dose today
radiation_msv.gap_note: 1 mSv/day is a DEMO ONLY limit. The live chart shows absorbed dose (uGy/h); converted to dose equivalent with quality_factor (1.0 = team default; real space radiation has a higher factor). Act now only from a solar particle event / shelter alarm (DONKI), never from a dose number.
radiation_msv.qa_note: QA 2026-11-14: 10 mSv/h should not be labelled ARS cutoff; mission limits depend on organ, duration, mission. | Use spacecraft radiation-alert and storm-shelter signals with mission-set limits, not a universal 10 mSv/h ARS rule.

qa.finding: QA 2026-11-14: 10 mSv/h should not be labelled ARS cutoff; mission limits depend on organ, duration, mission.
qa.recommendation: Use spacecraft radiation-alert and storm-shelter signals with mission-set limits, not a universal 10 mSv/h ARS rule.

actions.watch: Verify the environmental alert and mission-set radiation constraints; review shielding/EVA status.
actions.act: Follow the spacecraft's authorized solar-particle-event shelter warning and suspend EVA as directed.

sheet.baseline: Cumulative lifetime radiation exposure record maintained by NASA Radiation Health Officer
sheet.nominal: Background in LEO: 0.3 – 0.8 mSv/day (< 1.0 mSv/day nominal)
sheet.watch: Mission radiation warning / rising dose relative to mission-specific limits; 1mSv/day DEMO ONLY
sheet.act: Active spacecraft solar-particle-event or radiation shelter alarm (mission-defined); 10mSv/h is NOT an acute radiation syndrome diagnostic cutoff.
sheet.rationale: Operational storm shelter trigger during solar particle events; distinct from clinical ARS which requires high absorbed doses (>0.7 Gy).
sheet.escalation: Conditional; per rule branch and symptoms

radiation_msv.source: Medical lead's sheet (proposed, not clinically validated), RULE-16

symptoms._how_to_read: Red-flag symptoms the crew logs (Mood and symptoms log, daily check). Any of them = Act now. They also fulfil the Act-now rules marked requires_symptoms (e.g. RULE-05 irregular pulse WITH symptoms). A logged symptom counts for active_minutes.
